findings.issue_text: Migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11-13 crashes with NoMethodError on installs where the embed_category site setting row doesn't exist (Discourse only persists non-default values), so SELECT returns zero rows, [0] is nil, and nil['id'] raises; the uncategorized_category_id fallback is dead code and the unguarded [0]['value'] pattern at line 16 has the same flaw, blocking deploy

Migration line 29 interpolates the raw host value directly into the INSERT SQL; since host values are free-text from the old site setting and unvalidated, a value containing a single quote produces a broken INSERT, aborting the migration mid-flight with partially inserted rows and settings not yet removed

No category-destroy handling anywhere in the diff: deleting a category leaves orphaned embeddable_hosts rows, so ensure_embeddable passes, TopicEmbed.import calls PostCreator with a deleted category_id, and embedding fails with no admin-visible indication; no spec covers category deletion

Validation regex permits a port in host (example.com:8080), but record_for_host compares against uri.host which strips the port, so port-qualified stored hosts can never match any referer and embedding silently never works; no spec covers a port-qualified host

Admin EmbeddableHostsController destroy action calls nil.destroy when the id doesn't exist (stale tab, double-click, already-deleted row), raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of 404/no-op
The update action also crashes on a nonexistent id: nil is routed into save_host where host.host= is called on nil, raising NoMethodError

New controller specs only assert the controller is a subclass of AdminController; zero verification of create/update/destroy behavior or the embedding show/update serializer round-trip, and the embedding#update endpoint is an untested no-op that just re-renders while the client's saveChanges() calls embedding.update({}) against it with no template button and no server-side effect

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have swapped contents: category fabricator definitions live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and vice versa, which only works because Fabrication loads all files in the directory and will break on lazy-loading by filename or grep

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into lines (`records.each do |h|`), and then builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. There is no escaping/quoting helper used for `h`, so any value containing a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) will produce invalid SQL or worse. Even if the setting was typically constrained by the UI, the migration itself does not enforce/escape it, so a bad persisted value can make the migration fail at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No category-destroy handling anywhere in the diff: deleting a category leaves orphaned embeddable_hosts rows, so ensure_embeddable passes, TopicEmbed.import calls PostCreator with a deleted category_id, and embedding fails with no admin-visible indication; no spec covers category deletion

Validation regex permits a port in host (example.com:8080), but record_for_host compares against uri.host which strips the port, so port-qualified stored hosts can never match any referer and embedding silently never works; no spec covers a port-qualified host

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` validates `host` with a regex that explicitly allows an optional port `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`. The `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not remove the port, so a saved record can legitimately be `example.com:8080`. However `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) and compares with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. For a referer like `http://example.com:8080/...`, `uri.host` is `example.com`, which will never match a stored `example.com:8080`, making such entries unusable. Existing specs cover trimming scheme/path and host_allowed? for multiple hosts, but none cover port-qualified hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddableHostsController destroy action calls nil.destroy when the id doesn't exist (stale tab, double-click, already-deleted row), raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of 404/no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If no record matches (stale UI, double delete, etc.), `host` will be `nil` and `nil.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a 404 or graceful no-op. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The update action also crashes on a nonexistent id: nil is routed into save_host where host.host= is called on nil, raising NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record exists for that id, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately calls `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` instead of returning a 404 or validation error.

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6, the new plural hydration branch (`if (m[2])`) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and then unconditionally assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and `delete obj[k]`. If `_lookupSubType` returns nothing for an id (e.g., an ids list includes an id that wasn’t side-loaded into `root`), the resulting array will contain `undefined` entries, and the original `*_ids` list is removed so consumers can’t fall back to ids. This behavior is directly implied by the diff and is a plausible correctness defect; no tests in the diff cover the dangling-id case.

The finding asserts it “breaks” alignment, but that’s organizational/conventional and not a demonstrated correctness failure in this diff.

VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, but the `embeddable_hosts` site setting itself is removed and embedding host configuration is moved to the `EmbeddableHost` model/table. The remaining conditions (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`) still gate expansion to topics that actually have a `TopicEmbed`. So the finding’s claim that expansion is “no longer gated on any host being configured” is largely moot/intentional after the refactor, and the comment about the spec “passing vacuously only because embed_truncate defaults to false” is not verifiable from the provided diff (no relevant spec shown/retained here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 and :13-19 — validation allows port-carrying hosts like example.com:8080, but record_for_host compares uri.host (port stripped) against lower(host), so such hosts can never match and embedding is rejected with InvalidAccess

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The model’s host format validation explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and the `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not strip a port (e.g. `example.com:8080` remains). However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL/referer with `URI(...)` and compares `uri.host` (which excludes the port) against `lower(host)` in the DB. So a stored value like `example.com:8080` will never match an incoming `http://example.com:8080/...`, causing `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to return false and embedding to be rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:12-14 with config/routes.rb:139 and admin-embedding.js.es6:6 — the PUT #update endpoint and client saveChanges() perform no state mutation (embedding is an OpenStruct, not a store-backed model), creating dead API surface that silently discards staff PUTs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a singleton admin embedding resource wired end-to-end for PUTs: the Ember adapter for `embedding` targets `/admin/customize/embedding` and the client controller’s `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would issue a PUT. On the server, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (and `#show`) only `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` constructed in `fetch_embedding` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...`. There is no code in `#update` that reads params or persists any changes, so PUT requests are accepted but discarded. This is a verifiable dead/non-functional update endpoint as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:17-18 — params[:embeddable_host][:host] is accessed without a require/presence check, so requests without that payload raise NoMethodError (500) instead of returning a 400

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If a request omits the `embeddable_host` key (or it’s nil), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be `nil` and `[:host]` will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 instead of a controlled 4xx response. The diff adds this controller and contains no `require`/presence guard around that payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration builds SQL via raw string interpolation of stored setting values, allowing syntax errors or SQL injection from hosts containing quotes
Migration crashes when embed_category was never set because the query returns zero rows and the fallback is unreachable dead code

adjudication.rationale:
In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does:

```ruby
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i
```

If there is no `site_settings` row for `embed_category` (which is plausible when it was never explicitly set, since the DB may not store defaults), the `execute(...)` result set is empty, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises an exception. The later fallback `if category_id == 0` is never reached in that case, so the migration can crash exactly as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored host with a port can never match in record_for_host since uri.host never includes a port, making the validation-permitted example.com:8080 permanently unmatchable

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port in the stored `host` value (`...(:[0-9]{1,5})? ...`). The `before_validation` callback strips protocol and path but does not strip a `:port`, so a record can be saved as e.g. `example.com:8080`. However, `record_for_host` parses the referer/url via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host` (hostname only, no port) when querying: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Since `uri.host` will be `example.com` even when the referer is `http://example.com:8080/...`, it can never match a DB row stored as `example.com:8080`. Therefore port-bearing allowed hosts are effectively unmatchable despite being permitted by validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No UNIQUE index on host allows duplicate rows, making record_for_host's .first without ORDER BY nondeterministic

Therefore duplicate rows for the same host can be created. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` with no `ORDER BY`, so if duplicates exist the chosen record (and thus category via `TopicEmbed.import` using `eh.try(:category_id)`) is database-dependent/nondeterministic. This is a real correctness issue introduced/left by the diff.

If a category is deleted, existing `EmbeddableHost` rows can retain a now-invalid `category_id` (orphaned reference). Later, `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` as the `category:` for `PostCreator` while also passing `skip_validations: true`, so an invalid/deleted category id could be applied to newly created embedded topics/posts rather than being rejected. The “index” part is not what prevents orphans, but the lack of FK/existence validation is a real integrity/correctness risk introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Query on lower(host) is non-sargable and runs per embed request with no index on the hot path
